title: W4 gate ordering and continuation recovery
description: Acquire the ApplicationMutationGate lease as new_run/restore BEFORE issuing the transaction root or preparing an allocation candidate and hold it across the window (currently taken inside _run_participant_transaction, after the root is minted, intent committed, and allocation durably committed). Implement the forward-resume reconcile_startup actually requires: reacquire the owner implied by kind, recompute the deterministic allocation candidate, advance through participants_applying/participants_applied/completed, persist the typed failure diagnostic, and latch a fatal when recovery cannot be proven. Wire the abort/failure half (_advance_intent_to_abort, STAGE_ABORTED, _validate_failure, _apply_recovery_diagnostic, _replay_failure are all unreachable) so _rollback_transaction records failure and a failed transaction cannot strand a permanent record. ACCEPTANCE: tests proving a crash at each boundary RESUMES rather than merely reporting ok, and that a failed New Run leaves no unresolvable journal entry. Resolves B-C1 through B-C4.
close_reason: Fixed at d33816ee973cc4c39a0d2d87d216e8ccf1d7dc92. Lease is now acquired before the transaction root is minted or any allocation candidate prepared, and held across the window; reconcile_startup genuinely resumes forward (reacquires the owner, recomputes the allocation candidate, advances participants_applying -> participants_applied -> completed, persists typed failures, latches fatal when recovery cannot be proven); the abort path is reachable so a failed transaction reaches aborted with a typed failure and strands no record. Full suite 2054 tests, 2051 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending (baseline +7). All five crash boundaries proven to RESUME with assertions on journal completed plus live GameState.day, not merely on ok. Differential mutation proof: full revert 0/7, B-C1-only revert 5/7, B-C2/C4-only revert 2/7 - each fix's tests depend on it. DesktopContinuationOperationJournal.gd was untouched; its advance() state machine was already correct and only SaveManager orchestration was missing. SCOPE NOTE: _rollback_transaction still does not touch the journal on a FIRST-attempt live failure - the next reconciliation pass resolves it to completed/aborted/fatal instead. Also noted: FakeRestoreParticipant.gd has a permissive generic prepare() shape (left alone; unrelated suites depend on it) and the new tests use a locally-scoped shape-correct fake.

title: Plan-02 tail remediation: integration seams broken behind permissive test doubles
description:
Both whole-branch reviewers (2026-08-23) returned NOT READY on dwm-p2r.32's delivered work. Eight Criticals. ROOT CAUSE both reviewers independently identified: throughout the workstream the test doubles were MORE PERMISSIVE (publication ledger fake accepting kinds the real ledger rejects) or MORE CAPABLE (checkpoint fake implementing an idempotency/conflict law production lacks) than the production objects, so green suites certified behavior the shipped graph does not have. The suite is 2039/2042 green and the integration is still broken.

DESKTOP HALF (reviewer A):
A-C1 three of four production publishers cannot talk to the production publication ledger - DesktopPublicationLedger hardcodes KINDS minesweeper_round|shop_purchase|schedule_done and one uniform PUBLICATION_KEYS, but the frozen union is causal_sequence|action_source|board_fate with per-kind shapes; board-fate, shop and round publishers all send frozen kinds/shapes and DesktopActionReceipt has no receipt_id for the binding check. Bootstrap injects the same real ledger into all four. Fails AFTER the admission CAS, in the forward-only region.
A-C2 minesweeper_round departure fails at board-fate commit post-admission: the coordinator builds the departure request from the pre-completion board identity/revision, then commits the action source first, which adopts the NONE/identity-null/revision+1 projection into the shared board state; the fate port then re-checks the prepared pre-state against the changed live board and returns board_fate_conflict. Only the no_departure round path is covered by a real-port test.
A-C3 the consequence checkpoint tier is write-only: nothing in the tree reads desktop-consequence-checkpoint.json, and the stored ordinal-2 stage_candidate is a shape DesktopConsequenceState.validate rejects, so adding a reader would fail. No occupied-slot conflict law exists in the real SaveManagerCheckpointPort even though Task 8's ordinal safety rationale cites that law by name.

PERSISTENCE HALF (reviewer B):
B-C1 the ApplicationMutationGate lease is acquired AFTER the transaction root is issued and the identity allocation is durably committed, inverting the frozen law that requires acquiring new_run/restore BEFORE issuing the root; a busy or fatal-latched gate burns identity and strands the journal record.
B-C2 nothing resumes an incomplete continuation forward - reconcile_startup verifies and returns ok for every non-terminal stage without reacquiring the owner, recomputing the allocation candidate, advancing a stage, or latching fatal.
B-C3 SaveManager documents that a later reconciliation pass finishes a participants_applied operation; no such pass exists.
B-C4 the journal abort/failure half is unreachable from production, so each failed New Run burns an allocation AND appends a permanent unresolvable record - an unbounded durable leak compounding dwm-p2r.33.
B-C5 both sealed evidence documents carry red_green_command_records: [] and a dangling test_log_bindings path; the builder silently skips missing logs, the schema sets no minItems, and no test asserts non-emptiness, so --check reports OK forever.

Full finding text including Importants and Minors is in the SDD ledger at .godot/worktrees/dwm-p2r13-resealed/.superpowers/sdd/progress.md and in this session's review reports. Child beads carry the fix waves.

title: W6a behavioral divergences: abandonment, failure caching, lease span, validators, progress shape
description: Split from W6 (dwm-p2r.35.6) - the items that are real behavioral bugs rather than comments/cosmetics. From whole-branch reviewer A: A-I4 pre-admission abandonment is unimplemented so a restored pre-admission pending DEADLOCKS the desktop stack (plan line 2271 requires marking the durable unpromoted source checkpoint abandoned, releasing causal_transaction, committing no live participant; grep finds no abandon implementation, resume_pending hard-FAILS on a pending at action_prepared, bootstrap propagates that failure, and neither the shop nor the round path can clear it). A-I5 complete_round caches FAILURES so a transient failure is frozen forever while the ordinal-0 checkpoint and pending record are already durable - only cache on ok. A-I6 both action sources release the causal_transaction lease inside publish_recovery_action, which is callback 1 of a 3-callback departure plan, so board-fate publish, progress checkpoints and terminal cleanup all run UNLEASED - and DesktopBoardFatePort's own safety argument explicitly rests on the coordinator holding the lease across the whole prepare-to-publish span; release belongs after terminal cleanup, in the coordinator. A-I7 DesktopConsequenceState.validate_recovery_payload enforces a 4-key action payload while the coordinator overwrites recovery_payload at ordinal 1 with a 21-key admission-ready payload, so the public static REJECTS the payload its own coordinator writes for the whole post-ordinal-1 life of every transaction - make it a discriminated union on payload_phase or delete it. A-I8 publication_progress ships {cursor, complete, callback_receipts} while the frozen shape is {publication_plan_sha256, callback_ids, next_callback_index, callback_receipts}, so the frozen plan-hash-mismatch rejection rule is unenforceable and a resumed coordinator cannot detect a cursor belonging to a different plan.

title: New Run cannot complete against the real Profile and Localization participants
description:
FOUND 2026-08-23 by Plan-02 Task 9's crash-recovery suite, the first test to drive start_new_run through the COMPLETE real production graph (every prior test - test_new_run_transaction.gd, test_save_manager.gd - wires fake participants for every key, which is why this was never caught).

THE DEFECT. SaveManager.start_new_run() hardcodes two of its eight participant plans as caller-independent literals that bypass .prepare() entirely: plans[profile] = {profile: {}} and plans[localization] = {} (autoload/SaveManager.gd around lines 393-394). ProfileSchema.validate({}) rejects the empty profile candidate (ProfileSchema.gd:87 requires an exact 7-key object) and LocalizationManager._is_restore_plan_valid({}) rejects the empty localization candidate (LocalizationManager.gd:391-392 requires four keys). Unconditional: no profile.json content changes it, because the literal plan never reads _profile. Confirmed live for the profile half (participant order run -> desktop_consequence -> desktop_board -> PROFILE -> localization -> ... means profile fails first every time); the localization half is confirmed by code reading since the loop never reaches it.

WHY IT WAS DISCLOSED NOT FIXED. The adjacent comment states the intent - an empty profile patch is meant to PRESERVE the complete global profile for a new game - but LocalizationRestoreParticipant.prepare needs an explicit locale_id and ProfileRestoreParticipant.prepare needs a legacy_profile_patch_input. Deciding what start_new_run should supply, including the no-prior-profile.json fresh-install case, is product/design work Plan 02's brief never specifies. Task 9 proved it fail-closed, documented it at the source, and asserted it in DesktopAmendmentEvidenceGit.honest_gaps() (covered by test_desktop_crash_recovery.gd) so it cannot regress silently.

ACCEPTANCE. Decide the starting profile/locale semantics for a new run (including fresh install with no profile.json), wire start_new_run to supply real prepared candidates instead of the two literals, and prove a New Run completes end to end through the real ProfileManager/LocalizationManager pair - not fakes.
design: PRODUCT DECISION (user, 2026-08-24, controller session): Option A on both axes. (1) STARTING PROFILE: a New Run PRESERVES the complete global profile (preferences, gallery unlocks, input mappings, visited lines). Implement by routing the live profile through the real participant seam: plans[profile] built from _restore_participants[profile].prepare with legacy_profile_patch_input = {} (empty dict). prepare_legacy_profile_patch({}, {}) returns the live profile unchanged when migration_receipts.legacy_game_state_profile_v1 is already true, and a defaults-merged validated 7-key candidate otherwise; fresh install (no profile.json) therefore starts from ProfileSchema defaults. (2) LOCALE: chained from the prepared profile candidate preferences.language exactly as the restore path does at SaveManager.gd:1044-1047 - the profile prep returns locale_id, feed it to _restore_participants[localization].prepare. Fresh install gets schema default en. NO new initial_context key; _validate_new_run_context and all callers unchanged. IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: the honest-gap comment block at SaveManager.gd:448-461 must go; DesktopAmendmentEvidenceGit.honest_gaps() asserts this gap and is republished inside the sealed amendment documents, so fixing it drifts the amendment family and PAYS FOR A RE-SEAL - extract the bound-path sets from all four sealed documents first (as dwm-p2r.34 did) to confirm coupling, and fold the parked dwm-p2r.37 into that same re-seal pair. test_desktop_crash_recovery.gd currently asserts the fail-closed defect and must flip to assert the working path. Acceptance unchanged: prove a New Run completes end to end against the REAL ProfileManager/LocalizationManager pair, not fakes, including the fresh-install case.
notes: ADDENDUM (user decision via AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-24, dwm-p2r.33 implementation session): a THIRD caller-independent literal was unblocked by the profile/localization fix - start_new_run passed initial_context audio_context straight into plans[audio] = {snapshot: ...} without routing it through AudioRestoreParticipant.prepare(). The frozen _validate_new_run_context contract requires audio_context to be EXACTLY {}, but AudioManager._validate_snapshot requires the exact 4-key shape (music_context_id/music_context/ambience_context_id/ambience_context), so no caller - including the real MenuScene - could complete a New Run through the complete real graph, and a persisted new-run snapshot carrying audio_context {} would be unrestorable at the real audio prep. DECISION: Option A - the frozen {} already means a new run starts with NO audio context; translate it once inside start_new_run into AudioManager's own canonical empty snapshot (all four keys, empty ids = no music, no ambience), build the persisted RunSnapshot with the translated shape (keeping new-run saves restorable), and route plans[audio] through the real audio participant with the prepared profile candidate preferences, mirroring the restore path. Validator, callers, and initial_context keys all stay unchanged. No new honest gap is disclosed for audio because it is fixed in the same change.

title: complete_route_stage drops substage_id, so a substage is validated against the stage contract
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-context review of the dwm-p2r.14 route/presentation guard. Separate defect,
deliberately left out of that fix because it is a stage/substage confusion, not the
route/presentation one that fix was scoped to.

THE DEFECT. DayResolutionCoordinator.complete_route_stage builds the stage record it hands
_commit_completion as {stage_id, transaction_id} and drops substage_id, even though resume()
injects one into the command it registers. _commit_completion selects its validator on
str(stage.get(substage_id, )) != , so a substage arriving through the route door is validated
against STAGE_CONTRACTS[stage_id] instead of SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS[kind].
complete_presentation_stage forwards substage_id correctly; only the route door drops it.
The pre-check in complete_route_stage has the same blind spot.

WHY IT MATTERS. It fails closed one way and OPEN the other. A substage envelope hits a kind
mismatch, fine. But a STAGE-level envelope for a substage transaction passes _validate_envelope,
and RunLifecycle.complete_active_stage skips _validate_owner_receipt when record kind is
substage, so the substage contract is bypassed end to end.

REACHABILITY. Surviving-date presentations ARE substages: GameStateDayResolutionPort
_presentation_site routes substage ids prefixed surviving_date: to a dating presentation.
complete_route_stage has no production caller today, and the dwm-p2r.14 guard now steers every
production-shaped awaiting command to the presentation door, which handles substage_id
correctly. So this is latent AND newly masked, which is precisely why it is filed rather than
left in a note.

ACCEPTANCE. complete_route_stage carries substage_id through to _commit_completion and to its own
pre-check, so a substage completion is validated against SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS by kind through
either door. A RED test proves a stage-level envelope for a substage transaction is refused
before the fix and after it, rather than silently accepted. No change to the presentation door.

title: Prove the Hospital condition flag is checkpointed with the plan it belongs to
description:
RE-SCOPED on 2026-08-19. This bead was filed as a schema change and is now ONE TEST. The
original premise was wrong; see the 04:47 correction comment for the full withdrawal.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOW. Prove, rather than argue, that the Hospital condition flag and the
resolution plan are checkpointed and restored TOGETHER, so a resumed walk re-derives the same
P01.presentation.intent it already published.

WHY THE ORIGINAL PREMISE FAILED. The bead claimed a restore could produce a plan sitting
mid-Hospital beside a cleared pending_hospital, because _hospital_site() reads
should_route_hospital() live and resume() never re-runs begin_or_resume. It cannot. Both halves
come from the same bytes:

  * pending_hospital is a member of GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST.
  * capture_run_snapshot_input() builds gameplay from that whitelist and returns it beside
    lifecycle, which carries active_resolution_plan, in ONE dictionary.
  * GameStateDayResolutionPort._checkpoint_inputs() hands that one dictionary to
    RunSnapshotSchema.build, whose GAMEPLAY_FIELDS lists pending_hospital, producing ONE document.
  * GameState._apply_run_snapshot_silent() puts the lifecycle, the gameplay bag (through the same
    whitelist), the Contacts index and the committed aggregate back from that one document.

So persisting the derived required would have added a PLAN_KEYS member, from_dict validation, a
RunSnapshotSchema member and a migration branch to defend against a state the system cannot reach.
Neither Option A nor Option B is to be built.

THE REAL GAP, WHICH THIS BEAD CLOSES. Nothing asserted that atomicity. The safety of the resume
path rests on pending_hospital staying in _SAVE_WHITELIST and in RunSnapshotSchema's gameplay set,
and RunSnapshotSchema's gameplay check is an ALLOWLIST that rejects unknown members and says
nothing about a member that went missing. Every existing cut in
tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd restores from an in-memory
to_dict() and leaves the flag SET across the cut, so all of them would pass just as happily if the
flag stopped being captured at all.

ACCEPTANCE. One test in tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd that
crashes across the Hospital presentation, rebuilds the process from the ON-DISK checkpoint, and
proves the restored pending_hospital and the restored plan came back together -- so the intent
re-derives byte-identically BECAUSE the flag travelled with the plan rather than by luck. No
schema change, no new PLAN_KEYS member, and no DEVIATION-7.

NO LONGER BLOCKS dwm-p2r.15. The blocking edge was added on the withdrawn premise: a missing test
is not a reason to refuse to seal evidence, whereas an unfixed corruption was. Edge removed
2026-08-19.

DO NOT, STILL. Do not fix anything here by holding the answer in memory on the port, and do not
re-read live state anywhere on the resume path.

Neither carries pending_hospital nor the plan, so neither weakens what this test catches. Mutation-proved on both halves: dropping pending_hospital from GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST, or from RunSnapshotSchema.GAMEPLAY_FIELDS, must turn exactly this test red and name the cause. NO schema change, NO new PLAN_KEYS member, and NO DEVIATION-7. title: The reply-line closure law is never armed: configure_line_registry has zero production callers, so mark_line_visited admits any line id
description:
The reply-line closure law exists, is fully tested at its seam, and is NEVER ARMED in
production. Measured at 646f49e56249442209872123b1bb98f60b9f57c7 on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed in
worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-resealed during the Phase 01 Verification Gate run
(DEVIATION-16 on dwm-oyo.2). No byte was written; the tree was 0 dirty paths before and after.

THE CHAIN, EACH LINK MEASURED.

1. autoload/ProfileManager.gd:417 declares configure_line_registry(registry). A git grep for that
   name across every tracked .gd returns the one declaration plus 35 hits, and every single one of
   the 35 is inside tests/unit/test_dialogic_identity_registries.gd. ZERO production call sites.

2. autoload/ProfileManager.gd:438-440 is the whole admission predicate:
       func _line_registry_admits(line_id: String) -> bool:
           if _line_registry_fingerprint.is_empty(): return true
           return _line_registry_index.has(line_id)
   _line_registry_fingerprint is written only by configure_line_registry. Because nothing calls
   that in production, the fingerprint is permanently empty and the predicate is unconditionally
   true.

3. autoload/ProfileManager.gd:161-163 mark_line_visited therefore refuses ONLY the empty string.
   Its named refusal &"unregistered_line_id" at :163 is unreachable in production.

4. The live caller is autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:467, inside request_skip_step. It takes line_id
   from _runtime_adapter.current_line_id() at :456 and checks only is_empty() at :457. There is no
   registry check anywhere upstream of the write.

SEVERITY QUALIFIER, ALSO MEASURED, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN PATCHED IN PLACE.
current_line_id is defined in exactly one place tree-wide: tests/integration/test_dialogic_skip.gd:44,
a test fake. No production adapter defines it, and it is absent from
scripts/narrative/DialogicRuntimeAdapter.gd:18 REQUIRED_METHODS. So request_skip_step cannot complete
in production at all today, which is precisely what dwm-3an records. This is therefore a LATENT
fail-open, not a live one: it arms itself the moment dwm-3an is closed. Whoever closes dwm-3an must
close this in the same breath, or fixing the skip path will silently ship a global visited-history
writer that accepts any nonempty string as a line id.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG. The law itself is real and well proven at its seam.
tests/unit/test_dialogic_identity_registries.gd carries the command envelope, block closure, record
shape, empty and non-string line_id refusals, duplicate and widening refusals, and the
unregistered-id refusal. Measured GREEN this session at 2 scripts / 46 tests / 46 passing / 169
asserts, run together with tests/unit/test_art_manifest.gd. The defect is wiring, not law.

COST, PRICED AGAINST THE SEALS RATHER THAN ESTIMATED. Arming it needs one production call site plus
a fingerprint source (the parsed ids document already reaches ProfileManager's seam in the tests).
If the call site lands in autoload/DialogicBridge.gd, note that
evidence/phase_2r/handoff/desktop_contract.json binds that path from LIVE bytes with subject_commit
null, so ANY byte change to the bridge - a comment included - forces that handoff re-seal on its own.
evidence/phase_2r/schedule/gate.json does NOT re-seal: it hashes the bridge from its own frozen
subject commit 2bd24eb2ad0c4d76337cf0868257b77a7be666c0, not from the working tree. If the call site
lands only in autoload/ProfileManager.gd, no handoff contract binds that path and there is no
re-seal at all. Prefer the ProfileManager-only shape for that reason.

RELATED. dwm-3an (request_skip_step calls current_line_id, which the production adapter does not
define) is the blocker that keeps this latent. dwm-oyo.2 Phase 01 Verification Gate item 5 is the
gate line this sits under; its other four nouns - signals, atoms, visuals, context identity - were
measured closed and pinned in the same pass, and context's remaining field-level gap is dwm-n3h.

title: Specification 12.3 frozen-context field law is unenforced: frozen_context is a bare four-key Dictionary
description:
Measured during Phase 01 Task 7 (dwm-oyo.2, DEVIATION-15). Recorded because Ruling 14-C owes a bead for anything measured as genuinely unowned, and this is the one item of DEVIATION-14's DEFECT 9 that no plan claims.

WHAT THE SPECIFICATION REQUIRES. docs/design/2026-08-07-seven-day-dialogic-flow-design.md section 12.3 (line 1022) enumerates the frozen presentation context's applicable fields, gives a role-family table of REQUIRED frozen fields for eleven entry roles - ordinary message, solo invitation offer, group contact/offer, consequence/follow-up, solo pre-challenge, solo post-challenge, Hospital, pair pre-challenge scene, pair post-challenge scene, solo ending/exceptional step, P-L ending/Observer step and Alone step - and states the operative law: "Every concrete manifest entry expands the applicable row into one exact discriminated schema; it may add only fields explicitly enumerated for that entry and rejects every undeclared field." It also closes ending_form as an eleven-value union and forbids a sentinel friend, a fake Neutral attitude or a dummy tier for P-L and Alone.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ENFORCED, MEASURED AT autoload/DialogicBridge.gd. _PLAYBACK_CONTEXT_KEYS is exactly four - expected_stage, playback_id, role, transaction_id - and _exact_context_keys enforces only that exact four-key set on both start_entry and resume_entry. The record in data/manifests/dialogic_entries.json carries context_schema_id (for example context.ordinary_message.contact.ordinary.lavinia.day1.v1) and role, but NOTHING resolves context_schema_id to a schema and nothing validates a context against it. So the eleven role-family field lists, the per-entry discriminated schemas, the ending_form union and the no-sentinel rules are all unrepresented in executable code.

WHY IT IS NOT TASK 7's. Task 7's plan block cites 10.1, 12.4 and 14.3-14.4; 12.3 reaches it only transitively through the Task 5 bridge surface, and Task 7 types the prepared plan's frozen_context as a bare Dictionary exactly as the plan's own six-field block specifies. Task 7 DOES now type-guard the checkpoint's primitives at the restore trust boundary and refuses undeclared extra keys at the top level, but that closes the six-field plan shape, not the frozen context's interior.

WHY IT MATTERS. A restore or a start currently accepts any four-key context whose values are Strings, so a context that is wrong for its role - missing the fields its role family requires, or carrying fields its entry never declared - reaches Dialogic as a valid frozen context. DTL may branch on the frozen presentation context, so an unvalidated interior is a presentation-correctness hole, not merely a schema tidiness one.

LIKELY SHAPE OF THE WORK. Resolve context_schema_id through a published schema per entry, validate the frozen context against it inside the bridge's existing seam, and refuse with a named code. Note the blast radius before starting: DialogicBridge.gd is sha256-bound in evidence/phase_2r/handoff/desktop_contract.json and is one of the five ABSENT_SURFACE_SYMBOLS files, so every new column-zero public entry is +1 against the frozen tooling assert figure (14396 as of 646f49e56249442209872123b1bb98f60b9f57c7) and a handoff re-seal is owed in the same commit. Widening _PLAYBACK_CONTEXT_KEYS would move the frozen bridge-contract 1/14/14/275 and signal-boundary 1/30/30/244 baselines.

title: request_skip_step calls current_line_id, which the production adapter does not define
description:
MEASURED during the Phase 01 Task 6 pre-flight (DEVIATION-11 Finding 9) and re-confirmed 2026-09-01 at HEAD 2673550e47271fa9a638a7b821effc6a9096b9b7.

autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:456 request_skip_step reads its line id from _runtime_adapter.current_line_id() at :459. current_line_id is defined ONLY on the _FakeAdapter in tests/integration/test_dialogic_skip.gd:44 and is ABSENT from the production scripts/narrative/DialogicRuntimeAdapter.gd.

Today the defect is masked: configure_skip_context has no production caller, so the path short-circuits at :457-458 with skip_context_not_configured before ever reaching the adapter call. The moment anyone wires the skip context in production, that line becomes a hard runtime error on a method the production adapter does not define.

The wider entrance is unwired end to end. configure_skip_context is defined at DialogicBridge.gd:440 with three call sites, all inside tests/integration/test_dialogic_skip.gd. configure_narrative_bridge has NO caller anywhere - defined at scripts/ui/DialogueBox.gd:27, delegated at scripts/ui/DatingScene.gd:77-80, and nothing under autoload/, scripts/application/ or tests/ calls it. Separately, DialogicRuntimeAdapter.classify_next_event() returns the literal &"unknown" unconditionally at :134-137.

So mark_line_visited has ZERO reachable production writers at HEAD. This matters because it is the entrance that Phase 01 Task 6's visited-line identity law exists to guard, and specification 12.6 forbids exactly this class of identity - IDs are not derived from file path, line number, translated text, or label position.

NOT REPAIRED BY TASK 6. Ruling 12-B (maintainer-ratified 2026-09-01, recorded on dwm-oyo.2) lands configure_line_registry test-only precisely because wiring would edit autoload/ApplicationBootstrap.gd, which is sha256-bound in both handoff contracts, and would redden five legacy line literals including one inside the frozen profile-reset 3/3/102 baseline. Repairing the skip path is a separate production change with its own blast radius, and it should be sequenced with whichever task owns skip in production.
acceptance_criteria: DialogicRuntimeAdapter defines the method request_skip_step calls (or the bridge stops calling it), classify_next_event stops returning unknown unconditionally, and a test proves the production skip path end to end rather than through a fake adapter.

title: game_state_surface.json is 48 records stale and no gate detects it
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed at HEAD 2673550e47271fa9a638a7b821effc6a9096b9b7, tree clean.

evidence/phase_2r/runtime/game_state_surface.json does NOT reproduce from a clean HEAD. Regenerating it through the isolated runner with the generator's own mandated argument set produced digest 70f9346df83213d42ef57d4a52f6ad3b4b12aa7e93c9cdf7cf8a684e4cfb2ee8 against the committed d09fb54614ac6861f7a98ebff6719e4b0c9ae540ede5d309693f3267b9c1e089, with ZERO source edits in the tree.

SCALE OF THE DRIFT: 48 of 208 records differ, plus one entirely new dynamic_references key (request_schedule_done, 100 keys to 101). The staleness is old and wide - autoload/ApplicationBootstrap.gd call sites move by hundreds of lines (302 to 398, 672 to 834, 760 to 1261), autoload/SaveManager.gd 380 to 492 and 949 to 1085, and files that did not exist when the surface was generated now appear as call sites (scripts/application/desktop/GameStateDesktopConditionContextPort.gd, scripts/application/shop/GameStateMinesweeperShopPort.gd).

WHY NO GATE CATCHES IT. tests/unit/tooling/test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:1218-1219 compares the committed FILE's bytes against the digest stored in the committed RECORD (evidence/phase_2r/schedule/gate.json member generated_surface). Both are the same stale pair, so the assertion passes. Nothing in the repository re-derives the surface from live source and compares. tests/unit/tooling/test_public_surface_inventory.gd does build a live inventory over the real tree, but asserts signatures and dispositions, not call sites.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD. DEVIATION-11 Ruling D ordered Phase 01 Task 6 to regenerate the surface and re-seal its record in the same commit, on the belief that Task 6 would be what made it stale. That premise is false: the rot predates Task 6 by many commits and traces to none of its files. Ruling 12-A (maintainer-ratified 2026-09-01, recorded on dwm-oyo.2) supersedes Ruling D and leaves the file byte-untouched, so that this drift is repaired against its own honest commit boundary rather than folded into an unrelated exact-path commit.

title: Finish current scene-DTL validator diagnostics and CLI testability
description:
Deferred out of Phase 01 Task 3 sub-commit 3A (commit 3c4f28f0b8c5884f337ce32ee4969d8606b9798d). All items share ONE root: the Task 3 dialogic tooling declares laws that nothing reaches or enforces. None is blocking; all were measured, not argued.

PART A, THE THREE RESIDUAL MUTATION SURVIVORS. The final 76-site campaign at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-task3-campaign closed at 73 KILLED / 3 SURVIVED / 0 INVALID. The three survivors are G11 (the generator pre-write validation guard), C04 (the CLI per-master validate_file call) and C05 (the CLI non-zero exit branch). All three live inside the _run() of an extends SceneTree tool. Reaching them requires instantiation, and instantiating generate_master_skeletons.gd EXECUTES it and rewrites all eight masters from inside a test run, which is precisely why test_dtl_master_structure.gd preloads the generator and calls its static _build instead. A source-text assertion pinning those control-flow statements was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: this repository's text assertions pin published vocabulary (failure code names, count constants) where a rename must not pass unnoticed, and extending them to arbitrary statements would pin spelling rather than behaviour and read as coverage that does not exist. Both tools ARE exercised end to end by recorded manual runs (DIALOGIC_CONTRACT: PASS masters=8 entries=139 exit 0; GENERATE_MASTERS: OK 8 masters / 139 entries exit 0). Closing this needs a production seam that separates the decision body from the SceneTree entry point, the way _build is already separated, so a test can drive it without executing the tool.

PART B, FIVE FINDINGS FROM THE 3A FRESH REVIEWER, all independently re-confirmed against source by the controller before being recorded.

FINDING 1 SHOULD-FIX, tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd. CAUSAL_LINE and VARIATION_LINE are whitelisted then discarded; their PRESENCE is never required. Each constant appears only at its declaration and at one continue. A master with all 139 CAUSAL INPUT and VARIATION lines deleted validates CLEAN and validate_dialogic_contract.gd exits 0 on it, even though the file header presents the five-line block shape as law. The blank-line-count row of the whitelist is likewise unenforced, and an annotation appearing before the first label is silently swallowed. KNOWN LIMITS records none of this. THE MUTATION CAMPAIGN COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT: a check that does not exist cannot be mutated. Fix: record causal and variation presence in the block dictionary and emit DTL_ANNOTATION_MISSING for each absent one, then raise the count assertion in test_the_validator_rejects_a_block_with_no_annotations from 2 to 4 and assert both new message fragments. If the looseness is instead deliberate, amend KNOWN LIMITS so the header stops overclaiming.

FINDING 2 SHOULD-FIX, DtlStructureValidator.gd _classify. Four of the six sub-terms in the two hazard predicates are unreachable by any fixture; deleting the load-paren disjunct or any of the three call-branch terms survives the whole suite. Only V28 and V29, which got dedicated tests, die. Safety is unaffected because the closed whitelist still refuses the line; only the reported failure code is wrong. Fix: one fixture per uncovered term, each chosen so no other term also matches.

FINDING 3 SHOULD-FIX, tools/dialogic/generate_master_skeletons.gd. The generator opens whatever path the manifest names for WRITE with no containment check, while the read-only CLI has one. Its only guards are partition size 8 and total 139; DialogicEntryManifest.validate_document requires only a non-absolute res:// string, and the schema constrains locators.en.path to minLength 1. A wholesale retarget of one master group satisfies every guard, so the generator would overwrite the named file, project.godot included, and report success. The tool that WRITES has strictly weaker containment than the tool that only READS. Fix: share the CLI check before FileAccess.open, refusing unless the path begins with res://dialogic/timelines/en/ and the remainder holds no slash. THIS IS THE ITEM MOST WORTH DOING FIRST: three lines, plus one fixture, plus one campaign site.

FINDING 4 NOTE, tools/dialogic/validate_dialogic_contract.gd. begins_with(MASTER_DIR) accepts a legacy subdirectory path, so the CLI cannot detect the one manifest defect that would break the Ruling O partition it exists to protect: a master retargeted under a subdirectory would be collected by TimelineManifestBuilder and take timelines.json from 61 to 62. Fix as in Finding 3, same check.

FINDING 6 NOTE, DtlStructureValidator.gd. DTL_TRAILING_FALLTHROUGH reports lines.size(), always one past the last real line because every master ends with a newline. Fix: report the offending label's own line, consistent with every other block-scoped failure.

TWO FINDINGS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED HERE. Finding 5 (all 27 assert_string_contains calls pass a description into GUT's match_case parameter) changes no behaviour, since a non-empty String is truthy and match_case defaults true, and it is a pre-existing repo-wide pattern also present in test_day_resolution_coordinator.gd; it belongs to a GUT-usage sweep, not to this bead. Finding 7 (tools/evidence/capture_phase_2r_baseline.ps1 counts 69 English timelines where the sealed baseline.json records 61) is a SECOND unscoped walker of exactly the Ruling O shape, but baseline.json is immutable and digest-sealed by test_legacy_disposition.gd and nothing re-runs the script; record it wherever that script is next revived.

VERIFICATION OWED WHEN THIS IS CLOSED. Per the DEVIATION-4 CARRY-FORWARD, every law added here needs a campaign site that reaches it. Re-run the Task 3 harness at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-task3-campaign with new sites for each new branch, and re-run sites G11, C04 and C05 to prove they now die: a fixture without a site proves only that the suite is green. Then both frozen gates (25 scripts / 474 tests / 473 passing / 1 pending / 0 failing / 14396 asserts, and DOC_VALIDATION PASS packets=16 design_authorities=4 agent_workflow=1) and the four affected suites.

title: Ending label spelling diverges from spec: observation vs observer
description:
Two live ending labels in the English Dialogic tree carry a suffix the seven-day design never uses as
an ending identity. At HEAD the tree has ending.lavinia.observation and ending.priscilla.observation,
but docs/design/2026-08-07-seven-day-dialogic-flow-design.md section 13.8 names the stable identity
observer and enumerates the callable entries ending.lavinia.observer.full, ending.lavinia.observer.residue,
ending.priscilla.observer.full and ending.priscilla.observer.residue. The word observation appears in
the spec only as a common noun (pure-observation board, full-observation line), never as an ending id;
observer appears 49 times as the identity.

PROVENANCE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. Commit 9114351031ffd874b7079e6df12da915c4d27808 (Sun Aug 9 2026,
feat(dialogic): register exact timeline and narrative manifests) renamed all three retired .true labels
in one pass: ending.sylvia.true became ending.sylvia.special, which IS the spec word and maps cleanly
to ending.sylvia.special.full and .residue; ending.lavinia.true and ending.priscilla.true became
.observation, which is not. So the rename was internally inconsistent within a single commit, and only
two of the three labels drifted off the spec vocabulary.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY. The maintainer ruled on 2026-08-27 that the seven-day Phase 01 frozen
migration manifest (data/migrations/dialogic_61_to_8.json, dwm-oyo.2 Task 1) maps these two labels to
their .observer entries and records legacy_name_is_non_canonical on those rows, so the inventory keeps
the information rather than losing it. That ruling deliberately does NOT edit the .dtl files: Phase 01
Task 1 is inspect-only for the legacy tree, and a Global Constraint keeps the 61 legacy DTL and UID
files intact until Plan 06 proves the physical cutover.

WHAT REMAINS TO DO, AND WHEN. At the physical cutover the label written into the eight master timelines
must be the spec identity observer, not observation. Whoever performs the cutover must not carry the
legacy spelling forward. The frozen manifest rows are the record of the intended correspondence.

NOT AFFECTED, DO NOT CONFLATE. The three retired ending.*.true labels are a different matter and are
already correctly recorded with status rejected and never aliased to an Observer entry, per the plan
and per DEVIATION-2 on dwm-oyo.2. Bare label ending.priscilla_lavinia is also a different matter: it
names none of its three ending ids (.sweet, .dark, .observer) and stays unmapped by the same ruling.

title: A replayed substage completion never reports duplicate_transaction
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-context review of the dwm-p2r.20 fix plan.

THE GAP. The duplicate scan in prepare_completion walks active_resolution_plan[stages] and never
stage[substages]. A replayed SUBSTAGE completion therefore never reports duplicate: true. It falls
through to complete_active_stage, where _complete_record returns duplicate_transaction_conflict on a
differing receipt and a bare ok on an identical one.

CONSEQUENCE. A replayed substage returns stage_completed with a FRESH checkpoint rather than
duplicate_transaction. Every other seam in the coordinator is replay-idempotent and reports the
duplicate; substages silently are not. Present in the production port and mirrored in
tests/support/FakeDayResolutionStatePort.gd, so the fake would lie to any test that exercised it.

SCOPE NOTE. The dwm-p2r.20 tests deliberately avoid the duplicate path for exactly this reason.

ACCEPTANCE. The duplicate scan considers substages, so a replayed substage completion reports
duplicate_transaction and writes no second checkpoint, matching stage behaviour. RED proves the
current fall-through first. Fix the fake in the same change, or the unit suite cannot hold the claim.

REFERENCE. docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-20-p2r20-substage-contract-through-the-route-door.md

title: Carry contacts through the Minesweeper round transaction so group activation can commit
description:
Discovered 2026-08-17 while closing dwm-p2r.9 Step 2.5 coverage gaps on branch codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed.

Plan 06 Task 2 Step 2.4 item 7 requires the completion transaction to pass exact before/after round counts to ContactInvitationState so that only a 2->3 transition on Day 2/6 activates the group offer. That cannot happen today, and the cause is structural rather than a missing call.

GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST (autoload/GameState.gd:78-95) does NOT include the 'contacts' section. Consequences, both independently fatal:

1. GameStateMinesweeperPort._detached_clone() rebuilds its clone via reset_game() + apply_save_dict(to_save_dict()). Because to_save_dict() omits contacts, the clone always starts from DEFAULT contacts, so prepare_activate_group_after_round()'s 'both pair solos unread and AVAILABLE' predicate fails with missing_solo and never activates.
2. The port's candidate is exactly clone.to_save_dict(), which also omits contacts, so even a successful activation could never reach the committed candidate.

Verified empirically by probe on 2026-08-17: 'to_save_dict has contacts? false', 'candidate has contacts? false', receipt.group_activation_transaction_id = null, live group_action state after prepare = INACTIVE.

Therefore the hardcoded receipt values group_activation_transaction_id=null and message_transaction_ids=[] in GameStateMinesweeperPort.prepare_complete are TRUTHFUL for the current candidate surface. The real checkpoint port rejects the stub with invalid_checkpoint_inputs. Coordinator tests pass only because they use FakeCheckpointPort, which does not validate input shape.

Consequence: NO path persists a real ENDING or any snapshot to disk today. Direct scene path records no stable checkpoint (autosave returns no_stable_checkpoint, ignored); coordinator path cannot feed the real checkpoint port.

title: Choose narrative localization adapter after representative files exist
description:
## Rationale

Only English Dialogic timelines physically exist, while the user will supply already-localized narrative files later. Choosing an adapter before one representative source/translation set exists would assume an unknown physical format and could damage stable IDs, branches, or Dialogic round trips. Affected requirement: req.locale.narrative_deferred. This decision blocks translated narrative import only; it does not block Phase 2R UI localization or English narrative validation.

## Alternatives Considered

- Godot TranslationServer resources: rejected because the approved architecture uses the user's own localized files and custom JSON for UI localization.
- Preselect a duplicated-Dialogic-timeline adapter now: rejected until physical translated files prove their structure and stable-ID behavior.
- Test at least two adapters against representative files, then record the evidence-backed choice: selected decision process.

## Decision Trigger

Reopen active work when one representative English source and corresponding external localized files are present. Inspect their formats, stable IDs, branches, and round-trip requirements before proposing the adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Representative source and translated files are present; at least two viable adapters are tested against them; the chosen adapter preserves stable IDs, branches, and Dialogic structure without inventing prose; the decision packet records evidence and closes this issue.

title: prepare_completion declares a STAGE duplicate without comparing bytes, masking the conflict for stages
description: FOUND BY the dwm-p2r.22 fresh-context review, 2026-08-20, verified in source. GameStateDayResolutionPort.prepare_completion's stage branch (scripts/application/run/GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd:431-436) declares a duplicate on transaction id + completed state alone, with NO byte comparison against stage[receipt]. A completed STAGE replayed with DIFFERENT bytes therefore returns a benign duplicate carrying the stored receipt, and the domain's duplicate_transaction_conflict (DayResolutionPlan._complete_record:529) is unreachable for stages through this port. After the dwm-p2r.22 fix, SUBSTAGES are stricter than stages: the substage descent gates on _plan_receipt_from_envelope(receipt) == substage[receipt] and lets a mismatch fall through to the domain conflict. title: Deepen the seven shallow Task-1 RED obligations
description:
DECISION 7 allocated FULL table-driven depth only to the two atomic allocators, the crash cuts
around root commit, and the stale/conflict paths. Every other plan-line-797 obligation gets breadth
(at least one real assertion) in Step 1.1's behavioral half. Most are naturally complete at that
breadth. The seven below are NOT: they are clauses whose text plainly wants more than one case, and
they were deliberately truncated. This bead is the deliberate-later-deepening list DECISION 7
promised, per DECISION 9.7.

Do not deepen these before dwm-p2r.16 closes -- they would enlarge Step 1.1 past its session
budget and delay the .13/.9 unblock. Deepen after .16 closes and before dwm-p2r.9 consumes the
issuer boundary.

ROOT STORE -- tests/unit/test_desktop_issuer_root_store.gd

  Clause 30: schema rejection for missing/extra/malformed entries.
    Shipped: one representative case each of missing, extra, malformed.
    Wanted: a full table over every required root-document member
    ({schema_version,namespace,next_counter,receipts,allocation_receipts,
    day_advance_allocation_receipts}) crossed with missing / extra / wrong-type / malformed-value.

  Clause 34: rejection of deletion/replacement.
    Shipped: one deletion attempt and one replacement attempt.
    Wanted: deletion and replacement attempted independently against receipts, allocation_receipts,
    and day_advance_allocation_receipts, plus the no-op same-key identical replay that must SUCCEED
    (plan line 1682) rather than reject.

  Clause 35: rejection of a source/target receipt not byte-equal to receipts.
    Shipped: one mutated source receipt.
    Wanted: source and target independently, each mutated in every receipt member
    (receipt_id, purpose, namespace, counter, token, numeric_value), plus the absent-from-receipts
    case distinguished from the present-but-changed case.

JOURNAL -- tests/unit/test_desktop_continuation_operation_journal.gd

  Clause 36: external-journal exact schema.
    Shipped: the exact key set of a committed intent record.
    Wanted: the same missing/extra/wrong-type table treatment as clause 30, over both the document
    envelope and each operation record.

  Clause 38: every legal/illegal stage edge.  <-- LARGEST GAP
    Shipped: a representative subset -- intent_committed -> identity_allocation_committed, one
    skipped-index rejection, one illegal backward edge.
    Wanted: the complete stage adjacency matrix. Every ordered pair of stages asserted legal or
    illegal, crossed with the allocation-fields-nonnull rule (nonnull ONLY for the transition to
    identity_allocation_committed) and the participant-fields rule (nonnull ONLY for the exact next
    ordered participant). Plan line 780 says "every legal/illegal stage edge" and means it.

  Clause 43: startup forward reconciliation.
    Shipped: one successful reconcile_startup after a clean restart.
    Wanted: the irreversible-recovery diagnostic path in full -- a diagnostic recorded while
    next_stage == expected_stage at/after identity_allocation_committed with all allocation and
    participant fields null; proof it never relabels the operation terminal nor permits input;
    proof it clears ONLY after the original source/context proof succeeds byte-for-byte via
    load_context (DECISION 9.5); and proof that a DIFFERENT diagnostic conflicts.

  Clause 45: irreversible allocation retention.
    Shipped: one post-allocation rollback attempt returning retained state.
    Wanted: retention proven across each post-allocation stage, plus the plan-line-1714 law that
    rollback_silent() returns exactly {retained_allocation: true} and never decrements the counter
    or deletes receipts -- failed restore may burn identities but can never reuse them.

NOT ON THIS LIST, and why: clauses 28, 29, 31, 33, 42 (exact root key set, empty
day_advance_allocation_receipts default, capture detachment, persistence/reload, incomplete
listing) are complete at breadth -- each is a single law with a single shape, not a family of
cases. Clauses 1 and 8 ship as full breadth TABLES already (8 ordinary purposes; all 22 members of
the closed v1 child-kind union), so they are deep enough despite not being on DECISION 7's
depth list.
acceptance_criteria: All seven clauses (30, 34, 35, 36, 38, 43, 45) carry full table-driven coverage; clause 38 has the complete stage adjacency matrix; the focused p2r16 suite stays green; no new non-UID path is added to Task 1's frozen file map.
notes:
CORRECTION (dwm-p2r.16 DECISION 10.2, session 2 of 3, 2026-08-13).

Clause 45 above cites "the plan-line-1714 law that rollback_silent() returns exactly
{retained_allocation: true}". That half of clause 45 does NOT belong to
DesktopContinuationOperationJournal. Plan line 1714 assigns rollback_silent() to
DesktopIdentityAllocationRestoreParticipant, a TASK 6 restore participant, and the journal's frozen
seven-method surface at plan lines 707-714 declares no rollback method of any kind.

Do not look for it on the journal when deepening this bead. What the journal test file DOES ship for
clause 45, and what may be deepened here, is journal-side retention only: allocation_receipt byte-
equal across participants_applying / participants_applied / completed and across a recorded
irreversible-recovery diagnostic, plus refusal of any transition to `aborted` at or after
identity_allocation_committed (plan line 593). The rollback_silent() law is Task 6's to test.

this bead promised. Per DECISION 10.4 the session-2 file additionally walks the full eight-key

narrative) with the all-lower-nonnull / all-current-and-higher-null invariant asserted at each step,

DesktopIssuerRootStore continuation-allocation bundle is UNTESTED by the entire Task-1 RED set, not
merely shallow like the other seven. The root store's own tests assert replay-equality, changed-

members, one fresh root transaction receipt per remap source, and the single root candidate -- all

Both are production code written during Step 1.3 that no Task-1 test reaches. Same standing rule as

9. THE RESTORE transaction_remap TRIPLE IS UNVERIFIED (DECISION 14 FINDING D).
   Owning test: tests/unit/test_desktop_identity_nonce_issuer.gd,
   test_a_restore_bundle_proposes_source_plus_one_and_a_fresh_branch.
   Plan clause: line 1712 -- each restore entry is exactly {source_transaction_id,new_transaction_id,
   new_transaction_issuer_receipt}, keyed by source_transaction_id, the new receipt is purpose
   transaction_id, and its token equals new_transaction_id.

   DesktopIdentityNonceIssuer._with_transaction_remap therefore ships unverified, including the map

   the request's source set, and per entry that source_transaction_id equals the key, that
   new_transaction_issuer_receipt carries purpose transaction_id, and that its token equals
   new_transaction_id.

10. TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF THE CONTINUATION BUNDLE, ONE EXERCISED (DECISION 14 FINDING E; extends
    DECISION 13's FINDING A rather than replacing it).
    FINDING A recorded that DesktopIssuerRootStore._continuation_candidate is verified by nothing in
    Task 1: the root's own tests assert only replay-equality, changed-bytes conflict and
    superseded-counter conflict, and never inspect a bundle member.
    That is still true after session 3, and the picture is now wider rather than narrower. DECISION
    14.5 gave FakeDesktopIssuerRootStore a faithful hand-mirror of the same semantics, and the five
    issuer allocation tests exercise THE MIRROR. So the repository holds two implementations of the
    generation-zero / source-plus-one / one-receipt-per-remap-source law, and the green ones are the
    double's. A shared misreading of plan line 729 would be invisible.
    Depth wanted: assert bundle members against the REAL root store in

    run_id echoed from existing_run_id on restore and freshly minted on new_run, and exactly one
    transaction receipt minted per remap source in request order. That closes FINDING A and turns the
